tip: выглядишь (vyglyadish = you look) takes an adverb, not an adjective: классно (klassno = great) is the -о adverb form.
Russian drops the verb to be in the present; a dash links Зарплата (zarplata = salary) and пятьдесят (pyatdesyat = fifty).
In dates the month goes genitive: марта (marta = of March), so Восьмое марта (vosmoye marta) reads the eighth of March.
через (cherez) plus a time word means every other one: через день (cherez den) = every other day, not daily.
Floors take на plus the prepositional: на третьем этаже (na tretyem etazhe = on the third floor), never в (v).
который (kotory) changes gender to match its noun: Площадь (ploshchad) is feminine, so на которой (na kotoroy = on which) is feminine.
Тише (tishe = quieter) is the comparative of тихо (tikho = quietly), used alone as a command to be quiet.
Moving up a grade uses в plus the accusative: перешла в пятый класс (pereshla v pyaty klass = moved into fifth grade).
Quantity words push the next noun to genitive: полкило сыра (polkilo syra = half a kilo of cheese), not сыр (syr).
самый (samy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative: самый сложный (samy slozhny = the most difficult).
Some masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the prepositional after на (na): счету (schetu), from счёт (schet = account).
After десять (desyat = ten) the noun turns genitive plural: десять градусов (desyat gradusov = ten degrees).
люди (lyudi) has an irregular genitive plural людей (lyudey = of people), used after Сотни (sotni = hundreds).
Через (cherez) plus the accusative marks a future point: пять лет (pyat let = five years) counts forward from now.
метро (metro) never changes form; к ближайшему (k blizhayshemu = to the nearest) shows dative, but метро stays fixed.
бы makes a request polite and tentative: не могли бы вы (ne mogli by vy = could you) is softer than plain можете (mozhete).
